text:
Alana: Quick question – finalizing AWS KMS integration plan for Redwood Private (VPC). Two parts: control-plane keys (customer-managed CMK) and dataplane DEKs. How should we do credential exchange for the control plane so customer KMS never sees our long-lived creds?

Miguel: Short answer: use IAM role assumption + sts:AssumeRole external-id pattern. Control plane uses a short-lived session that has kms:Encrypt/kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey via a customer-created role. Customer grants our account via a trust policy.

Alana: Can you drop the minimal trust policy and the kms key policy bits? I want to hand to customers as an example.

Miguel: Sure – here's a compact example (customer side) for the KMS key policy + role trust. Paste into docs as-is but warn about principals.

Miguel: ```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDDIT_CONTROL_PLANE_ACCOUNT_ID:role/RedwoodControlPlaneAssumeRole"},
      "Action": "kms:Encrypt",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

sophia: small nit – don't give kms:CreateGrant in key policy. Instead grant via IAM role + customer can create grants for DEK rewraps. Also add conditions for "aws:SourceVpc" if they want to limit to their VPC endpoints.

Ryan: For dataplane DEKs: we recommend envelope encryption where dataplane instances use local DEK cache, DEKs are generated via GenerateDataKey (without plaintext in logs). Rotation flow we suggest: monthly DEK rotation + background rewrap: use ReEncrypt with DestinationKeyId = new CMK. Also ensure audit logs include KMS Event logging.

Alana: audit logging — do we want them to enable CloudTrail key events with management & data events? Also give them sample CloudTrail insight query to find failed decrypts.

Miguel: Yes. Ask customers to enable CloudTrail logging (Write + Data events for KMS). Example Athena query for failed decrypts:

Miguel: ```sql
SELECT eventTime, userIdentity.principalId, eventName, errorCode, requestParameters
FROM aws_cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventSource = 'kms.amazonaws.com' AND errorCode IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY eventTime DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

sec-bot: Reminder: don't log plaintext DEKs or GenerateDataKeyPlaintext outputs to any logs. :warning:

Alana: One more—key rotation handoff for on-prem Private. If customer rotates CMK, how do we ensure dataplane rewraps don't blow up? Proposed handshake:
- Customer creates new CMK and marks it as "rotation-pending"
- They call Redwood control-plane endpoint to register new key ARN
- Control plane schedules ReEncrypt jobs on dataplane nodes with backoff and can fallback to last-known-good KEK via grants

sophia: add explicit 'CreateGrant' step and store grantId in our key metadata so control plane can revoke or reissue grants during rotation.

Ryan: Ops note: when rewrapping at scale, prefer batch ReEncrypt with continuous batching to avoid KMS rate limits. Add retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

Alana: Thanks — I'll draft the short customer-runbook and post in docs. tagging @miguel @sophia for review. :thumbsup:

miguel: Looks good to me. small comment: include sample CLI commands for sts assume-role and GenerateDataKey without plaintext.

Miguel: ```bash
# assume role
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodControlPlaneAssumeRole --role-session-name rp-session --external-id EXTERNAL123

# server-side GenerateDataKey (ciphertext only pattern)
aws kms generate-data-key --key-id alias/customer-kek --key-spec AES_256 --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 -d > dek.cipher
```

Alana: perfect, will add. End of thread.
